Practices and references

An original operational interpretation of the three reference lenses.

Published from main · 498c0f3View source ↗Propose an edit ↗

Purpose

An original KDV interpretation for operational use. These connections are illustrative, not an official equivalence, assessment or reproduction of the source frameworks.

Working sequence

ReferencePractice lensKDV operational expressionEvidence
DAMA-DMBOK 2Governance and accountabilityNamed owners and scoped decision rights.Role register and decision record.
DAMA-DMBOK 2Metadata and qualityShared definitions, product context and quality rules.Glossary, lineage and test results.
DAMA-DMBOK 2Security and operationsClassification, authorised access and recovery practices.Policy record and recovery check.
DCAMCapability developmentAgree priorities, assign responsibilities and review improvements.Action backlog and accountable follow-up.
DCAMEvidence of practiceDemonstrate execution and outcomes over time.Decisions, controls and indicator trends.
Data MeshDomain ownershipHives and Cells own their products and meaning.Domain and product charters.
Data MeshData as a productVersioned contracts and consumer-oriented delivery.Contract, feedback and usage.
Data MeshSelf-serve infrastructureReusable delivery paths with clear operating boundaries.Service interface and operational checks.
Data MeshFederated computational governanceCommon rules, local decisions and automated checks where feasible.Baseline, policy tests and exceptions.

Original references

  • DAMA-DMBOK 2: The data management knowledge reference informing the governance vocabulary.
  • DCAM: A capability framework informing evidence-led improvement. Consult its publisher for access and licensing.
  • Data Mesh: The four principles informing domain ownership, data products, self-service and federation.

Scope and limitations

KDV adds an original operating interpretation. DAMA-DMBOK and DCAM material is not redistributed. References do not imply endorsement, affiliation, certification or an official mapping.
